# Psalm 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. With-stringed-instruments. A-psalm of-David.

**2** When-I-call, answer-me, O-God of-my-righteousness. In-distress You-have-made-room for-me. Be-gracious to-me and-hear my-prayer.

**3** O-sons of-man, how-long [shall] my-glory [be turned to] shame? [How long] will-you-love emptiness, will-you-seek falsehood? Selah.

**4** But-know that YHWH has-set-apart the-faithful-one for-Himself; YHWH hears when-I-call to-Him.

**5** Tremble and-do-not sin; speak in-your-hearts upon-your-beds and-be-still. Selah.

**6** Offer sacrifices-of righteousness, and-trust in YHWH.

**7** Many [are] saying, 'Who will-show-us good?' Lift upon-us the-light of-Your-face, YHWH.

**8** You-have-put gladness in-my-heart, more-than [when] their-grain and-their-new-wine abound.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **4:5**: The Hebrew rogzu can mean 'tremble' or 'be agitated.' The LXX translated it as orgizesthe ('be angry'), which Paul quotes in Ephesians 4:26.

— EMET
